title: U.S. House · Connecticut's 4th District
area: Fairfield County, including Greenwich, Stamford, Norwalk, and Bridgeport

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Jim Himes advanced unopposed. Michael Goldstein defeated Daniel Miressi in the Republican primary. Damon Cerreta is running as an independent. The Cook Political Report rated this district D+13 based on 2024 presidential results.

summary.text: Jim Himes is the Democratic incumbent for Connecticut's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2008. A former Goldman Sachs vice president, he serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where he was ranking member in the 2023–2024 Congress.

background.text: Born in Lima, Peru; earned a bachelor's degree from Harvard University in 1988 and a master's degree from Oxford University in 1990.
Worked as a vice president at Goldman Sachs and later at the affordable-housing nonprofit Enterprise Community Partners before entering politics.
Served on the Greenwich, Connecticut housing authority from 2003 to 2006, chairing it, and on the Greenwich board of estimate and taxation from 2006 to 2007.
Has represented Connecticut's 4th District in the U.S. House since 2009, currently serving his ninth term.

priorities.text: Says every American should have access to high-quality, affordable health care, and that Congress needs pragmatic, innovative solutions to expand coverage and decrease costs.
Says the federal government must defend access to comprehensive reproductive health care and ensure every individual can make their own medical decisions free from political interference.
Says gun violence prevention measures, consistent with Second Amendment rights, are necessary responses to mass shootings and everyday gun violence.

positions.summary: Has long supported the Women's Health Protection Act, which would bar medically unnecessary restrictions on abortion and write abortion-access protections into federal law.
positions.quote: I have been a longtime supporter of the Women's Health Protection Act, which would prohibit medically unnecessary requirements or restrictions on abortion services, enshrining protection to abortion access into federal law.

positions.summary: Supports expanded state crisis intervention (red flag) laws, funding for community violence intervention, enhanced background checks for people under 21, and penalties for straw purchases and firearms trafficking.
positions.quote: I support expanded state crisis intervention programs (including Red Flag Laws), funding for community violence intervention programs and mental health services, enhanced background checks for individuals under 21, and penalties for straw purchases and firearms trafficking.

positions.summary: Says the urgency to transition to clean energy has never been greater and supports putting a price on carbon to boost renewable energy and cut greenhouse gas emissions.
positions.quote: The urgency to transition to clean energy has never been greater.

positions.summary: Says Congress needs to expand health care coverage and decrease costs, and has supported measures expanding health insurance subsidies and Medicare and Medicaid eligibility.
positions.quote: Congress needs to find pragmatic, innovative solutions to expand healthcare coverage and decrease costs.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 2025–2026 Congress.
Served as ranking member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence in the 2023–2024 Congress.
Chaired the Financial Services Subcommittee on National Security, International Development and Monetary Policy in the 2021–2022 Congress.
Sponsored and supported multiple War Powers Resolutions this Congress seeking to require withdrawal of U.S. military personnel from unauthorized conflict with Iran.

candidates.name: Michael Goldstein
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Daniel Miressi in the August 11, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Michael Goldstein is the Republican nominee for Connecticut's 4th Congressional District. He is a physician and attorney who has run for this seat in previous cycles. He has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Harpur College at Binghamton University (1970), an M.D. from SUNY Downstate Medical School (1974), and a law degree from the Elisabeth Haub School of Law at Pace University (2006).
Has previously run for Connecticut's 4th Congressional District, including in the 2024, 2022, and 2020 election cycles.

summary.text: Damon Cerreta is an independent candidate for Connecticut's 4th Congressional District. A Stamford-born business owner, he is running on themes of reducing corporate abuses of consumers and strengthening working-class protections.

background.text: Born in Stamford, Connecticut; earned a high school diploma from Ridgefield High School.
Has worked as a business owner, including managing a customer service team before starting his own company.

priorities.text: Proposes legislation to eliminate hidden fees and price increases in service agreements and to stop companies from locking customers into unfair multi-year contracts.
priorities.quote: I propose new legislation that will: Eliminate hidden costs and uncontrollable price increases in service agreements. Prevent corporations from locking customers into unfair multi-year agreements. Protect customers from being sued if they try to leave an agreement that was misleading or materially altered by the service provider. Stop the cycle of corporations raising prices and pushing out small businesses.

priorities.text: Says he is passionate about economic, healthcare, education, veterans' affairs, and environmental policy, and wants to expand access to quality healthcare and educational opportunity.
priorities.quote: I'm passionate about economic, healthcare, education, veterans and military affairs, foreign, environmental, and social policy. I believe in supporting working families, expanding access to quality healthcare, and ensuring every child has equal educational opportunities.

priorities.text: Calls for greater civic engagement and bipartisan common ground, citing what he sees as growing national division as one of the country's biggest challenges over the next decade.
